description: Hooks add predictability/guarantees to the-loop's PDLC process. SessionStart surfaces the project's config; PostToolUse records a pull request the session just opened against its work item (`the-loop sessions link-pr`), so the work item's tracking is a fact the-loop wrote rather than one it inferred (issue-370); Stop runs the-loop's gate wrapper, which asks `the-loop check` whether the current graph node is complete and blocks the stop when it is not (issue-109). Both wrappers are Python, stdlib-only, so they run on Windows too. The harness hook is a CLOCK — it says when to look; the graph says what we are looking at, so the wrapper never needs to know which phase the work item is in. In Cursor the gate wrapper ships via .cursor/hooks.json, returning a followup_message instead of blocking; Cursor has no PostToolUse equivalent, so there the skill's prose rule remains the way a pull request is recorded. Quality gates (lint/typecheck/test) are documented for projects to wire to their own tooling, since commands are project-specific.

hooks.command: test -f .the-loop/harness-config.yaml && echo 'the-loop is initialized in this repo. Operating rules: plan→execute→self/critic-review→escalate. Read .the-loop/harness-config.yaml (the agent config; the CLI never reads it) and follow the the-loop skill.' || true
